domain: control theory, cybernetics, and OODA loop doctrine
axioms: A phase exists only if deleting it changes the loop's transfer function; a box whose removal leaves every edge intact is a label, not an operation.
Every loop element must have a decidable trigger predicate over named loop state, otherwise it cannot be scheduled, audited, or starved-detected.
Coupled loops at different pace layers exchange shear; any element that can fire at multiple layers must specify cross-layer containment or it will thrash the slow layer.
Inserting an element upstream of Act adds deadtime, and deadtime plus feedback is the classic source of oscillation between exploration and exploitation.
Speculative output re-entering the sensing stage is a positive-feedback path unless attenuated by an enforced marker at the boundary.
Requisite variety must be supplied by some regulator; if OODARC under-serves exploration, the deficit is either a missing element or an under-specified Orient, and those are distinguishable.
Orchestration topology is only orthogonal to phase structure while no phase is intrinsically multi-agent.
primitives: feedback sign (negative regulation vs positive runaway)
failure_mode: Treats well-formed loop structure as sufficient — a candidate can be topologically perfect and still be a bad concept, an unearned name, or epistemically unsafe.
Undervalues human/practitioner factors: memorability, teachability, and whether anyone will actually invoke the element.
Prone to accepting a formalizable-but-useless element because it diagrams cleanly, and to rejecting a fuzzy-but-generative practice because its trigger cannot be written as a predicate.
Blind to storage and retrieval semantics — sees the re-entry edge but not what persists, who cites it later, or how it expires.
Can mistake control-theoretic analogy for evidence, importing stability language where no measurable gain or delay exists.
